column4: note
Coastal Corp was bought by El Paso on 2001-01-29; later prices under CGP are a different instrument (they run to 2022)
Hercules was bought by Ashland on 2008-11-13; afterwards the price is frozen at $30.02 with no volume and later becomes another instrument

Williams: EODHD's dividend adjustments are far too large (adjusted +105% vs traded and Yahoo +66% in 2004); dividends were about $0.01 a quarter. It records $0.56 dividends on 2002-07-30, 2002-10-30 and 2003-01-29 (adjustments of +33%, +45%, +18%), so the exclusion starts there (moved from 2003 in M5c)
Johnson Controls: 2016 merger with Tyco and Adient spin-off; EODHD's adjusted return (+64%) disagrees with its traded price (+38%) and Yahoo (+42%), so 2016 can't be trusted
Mylan became Viatris on 2020-11-16; the last two prices under MYL are $0.079 (traded and adjusted), a fake -99.5% for anyone holding it
DowDuPont became DuPont (DD) on 2019-06-03; the code then carried DD's prices, but its last print is $30.52 the day after $74.11 while DD traded at $75: not a real price

St. Jude Medical: EODHD's traded prices already include the 2002-07-01 2-for-1 split and the adjusted prices apply it again: a fake +86% on the split day. Three weeks blanked, so a holder exits at the last correct price (flagged) instead

US Steel: EODHD records a 2-for-1 split on 2005-05-13 that never happened (the traded price fell 3%): a fake +94% in the adjusted price. Three weeks blanked, so a holder exits at the last correct price (flagged) instead
Golden West Financial: from 2003-03-05 EODHD's GDW is a different instrument (traded $71 -> $2.20, then penny-stock prices), while Golden West traded around $70-100 until Wachovia bought it in 2006

Transocean: on the GlobalSantaFe merger day EODHD's adjusted price jumps +30%, but holders got 0.6996 new shares plus $33.03 cash per share, worth less than the old share. Three weeks blanked, so a holder exits at the last pre-merger price (flagged) instead

First Data: the Western Union spin-off (2006-09-29) is missing from EODHD's adjusted prices, a fake -44% day. Three weeks blanked: it isn't ranked on the fake loss, and a holder exits at the pre-spin-off price
Cablevision: the AMC Networks spin-off (2011-06-30) is missing from EODHD's adjusted prices, a fake -28% day. Three weeks blanked, as for First Data

American Capital: EODHD records a $1.07 dividend on 2009-06-18, a third of the $3.27 share price, and adjusts +36% for it; the company paid no dividends in 2009 (suspended in its 2008-09 debt crisis). Three weeks blanked, so a holder exits at the last correct price (flagged)

Time Warner: EODHD's prices before 2003-10-16 are on a different split basis (x3, as if adjusted for the 2009 1-for-3 reverse split) than after: a fake -66% day. Three weeks blanked, so a holder exits at the last price before it (flagged)
R. R. Donnelley: until 2001-12-18 EODHD's series sits around $0.02 a share (the company traded around $30), then jumps 44,281% in a day. Found in M6, when a momentum variant held it across the jump
Gateway: the September 1999 2-for-1 split is applied twice (adjusted +92% while the traded price fell 4%). Three weeks blanked, so a holder exits at the last price before it (flagged). Found in M6

Kansas City Southern: the July 2000 spin-off of Stilwell Financial (Janus) is missing from the adjusted prices, a fake -97% day. Three weeks blanked, so a holder exits at the last price before it (flagged). Found in M6
Raytheon: adjusted price 372 -> 18.7 on 2001-05-14 while the traded price stayed at about $29.5. Three weeks blanked, so a holder exits at the last price before it (flagged). Found in M6

Liz Claiborne (code KATE): the January 2002 2-for-1 split is applied twice (adjusted +102% while the traded price barely moved). Three weeks blanked, so a holder exits at the last price before it (flagged). Found in M6

Electronic Arts: prices before the November 2003 split are on a different scale (traded $775 -> $46), a fake -88% day. Three weeks blanked, so a holder exits at the last price before it (flagged). Found in M6
St. Jude Medical: the November 2004 2-for-1 split is applied twice, as in 2002 (adjusted +106%). Three weeks blanked, so a holder exits at the last price before it (flagged). Found in M6
Schering-Plough: from 2008-01-08 EODHD's series is junk ($2.50 on zero volume for five months, then a different $9 instrument) while the real stock traded around $20. Found in M5c and M6

E.W. Scripps: the July 2008 spin-off of Scripps Networks is missing from the adjusted prices, a fake -93% day. Three weeks blanked, so a holder exits at the last price before it (flagged). Found in M6
Questar: the June 2010 spin-off of QEP Resources is missing from the adjusted prices, a fake -67% day. Three weeks blanked, so a holder exits at the last price before it (flagged). Found in M6
Noble Energy: the May 2013 2-for-1 split is mishandled (traded 236 -> 59), a fake -50% day. Three weeks blanked, so a holder exits at the last price before it (flagged). Found in M6
